message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work independently, so I'll check the refund ledger against W2's handoff claim.
The refund ledger matches W2's handoff exactly, with the same two order IDs and amounts. Next I need the order list to identify the customers in the batch before pulling their net balances.
The refund ledger matches W2's handoff exactly, and the orders identify three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 5519 cents. The refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff, so I'll continue with the next customer, birch.
Acme and birch have net balances, and the refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff. The last customer in the batch is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance before recording any payouts.

I checked the arithmetic: acme's orders (15695 + 4370) less refund 250 (14546) is 5519, birch's orders (2763 + 12355) less refund 251 (1481) is 13637, and cobalt's orders (36165 + 17659) with no refunds is 53824. All three match net_balance, and the refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff, so there's no reason to hold. Recording the first payout, for acme.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch and cobalt remain, and their balances and the refund ledger have already been checked against the orders, so I'll record birch's payout next.
Birch's payout is recorded, and cobalt is the last customer left. I already verified cobalt's 53824 against its orders (36165 + 17659) with no refunds, so I'll record that payout now.
All three payouts were recorded successfully. Each amount matched net_balance and was checked against the orders and the refund ledger, which matches Alpha's handoff.
